transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I keep getting these sudden, vivid memories of the train crash that pop into my head and completely derail whatever I’m doing. It happened a little over two years ago, and I've tried to just power through, but they are completely disrupting my life now.
Have these flashbacks been happening for more than one month, and have they started within the first month after the crash?

Yes, they've been happening pretty much continuously for over two years now, so definitely much longer than a month. They actually started within the first few weeks right after the crash, but back then I just tried to ignore them and power through my work.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F43.10", "F43.0"], but based on this conversation, F43.0 (Acute Stress Reaction) is no longer likely because the symptoms have persisted for over two years and started within weeks of the trauma, which exceeds the typical short duration (minutes to days) of Acute Stress Reaction. The persistent and intrusive flashbacks occurring for more than one month and beginning shortly after the traumatic event align with F43.10 (Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder). No other differential diagnoses are currently indicated based on the information provided.

inference_history.note: The patient describes sudden, vivid, and intrusive memories related to a traumatic event (train crash) occurring over two years ago, which is disrupting daily functioning. This presentation strongly suggests a trauma-related disorder. The primary candidates are F43.10 (Post-traumatic stress disorder, unspecified) due to the re-experiencing symptoms and functional impairment, and F43.0 (Acute stress reaction) though less likely given the two-year duration. However, F43.0 typically presents within hours or days of trauma and lasts less than one month, so it remains only as an initial consideration. No other candidates are currently warranted based on available information.
